items.headline: Update: ASEAN summit opens in Manila with Singapore due to take the 2027 chair
items.summary: Southeast Asian leaders, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong among them, opened the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, with the South China Sea, Myanmar's civil war and trade topping the agenda. Singapore will assume the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027, and US President Donald Trump is due later in the week to press the bloc to join his ‘Pax Silica’ chip-security pact.

items.headline: India's October trade deficit widens to a one-year high of $39.88 billion
items.summary: India's goods trade gap jumped to $39.88 billion in October, the widest in a year, as festive-season gold imports roughly tripled to about $5.51 billion and the oil-import bill climbed 54% from a year earlier. The figure overshot a Reuters poll forecast of about $32 billion, though it stayed below October 2025's record of $42.58 billion.

items.headline: Israeli strike kills a senior Hamas commander in Gaza despite the truce
items.summary: The Israeli military said it killed Samir Abu Younis, commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, in an overnight strike in southern Gaza — the latest in a run of targeted killings that have continued since the October ceasefire. Gaza's Health Ministry says Israeli fire has killed more than 1,600 Palestinians since the truce took hold.

items.headline: Update: US floats letting Ukraine join NATO if it cedes the rest of Donbas
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had raised a proposal under which Ukraine could gain NATO membership in exchange for handing Russia the roughly one-fifth of Donbas it does not already control — a swap Kyiv has long called a red line. The idea surfaced after US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi produced only a prisoner exchange.

items.headline: Anthropic heads for a landmark Nasdaq debut this week
items.summary: AI developer Anthropic is set to price its initial public offering on Nov 18 and start trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ‘ANT’ on Nov 19, in one of the largest tech listings on record. A sale of about 825 million shares at $70-$78 implies a valuation near $1.4 trillion, down from the roughly $2 trillion once floated before this autumn's AI-stock wobble.

items.headline: SpaceX catches a returning Starship at the launch tower for the first time
items.summary: SpaceX recovered the upper stage of its Starship rocket by catching it with the launch tower's mechanical arms at Starbase, Texas, after a 22-hour orbital flight that deployed Starlink satellites — a first for the programme and a step toward full reusability. The Super Heavy booster was lost earlier in the flight, denying the company a planned double catch.

items.headline: 🏏 India beat New Zealand by 22 runs to clinch the ODI series 3-1
items.summary: India defended a modest 209 to win the fifth and final ODI at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, by 22 runs, taking the series 3-1. Arshdeep Singh (3-30) was named player of the match as India sealed their first away ODI series win in New Zealand in seven years and ended the hosts' long unbeaten home run.

items.headline: 🎾 World No. 1 Zverev opens his ATP Finals campaign with a 6-4, 6-4 win over Jodar
items.summary: Alexander Zverev, the new world No. 1 and top seed, began his Nitto ATP Finals Group A campaign in Turin with a composed 6-4, 6-4 win over Rafael Jodar, striking 10 aces and never facing a break point. Defending champion Jannik Sinner is missing the event through injury.

items.headline: 🏎️ F1 heads to Las Vegas with Verstappen favourite and the fight for second wide open
items.summary: With Kimi Antonelli already crowned champion and Mercedes holding the constructors' title, Formula 1's penultimate round on the Las Vegas Strip (Nov 21) centres on Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton and George Russell scrapping over runner-up honours. It is the first Las Vegas Grand Prix run under 2026 rules, which drop DRS for active aero and an ‘Overtake Mode’.

fun_fact.headline: The Canary Islands are named after dogs, not birds
fun_fact.body: The Canary Islands are named after dogs, not birds. The name comes from the Latin Canariae Insulae, ‘Islands of the Dogs’ — the Roman writer Pliny the Elder recorded that the main island teemed with large dogs. The little yellow canary bird, and the colour, were later named after the islands, not the other way around.
fun_fact.source: Britannica; Pliny the Elder, Natural History

puzzle.title: Two Candles
puzzle.body:
Two candles of the same height are lit at the same moment. One burns down completely in 4 hours, the other in 3 hours, each at a constant rate.

After how long is one candle exactly twice as tall as the other?
puzzle.approach: Write each candle's height as a fraction that falls at a steady rate, then set one equal to twice the other.
puzzle.answer:
2 hours 24 minutes.

Let each candle start at height 1. After t hours the slower (4-hour) candle has height 1 - t/4; the faster (3-hour) candle has height 1 - t/3, so the slower one is always taller.

Set slower = 2 x faster:
1 - t/4 = 2(1 - t/3)
1 - t/4 = 2 - 2t/3
Multiply by 12: 12 - 3t = 24 - 8t
5t = 12, so t = 2.4 hours = 2 h 24 min.

Check: slower = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4; faster = 1 - 0.8 = 0.2; and 0.4 = 2 x 0.2. Both are still burning (t < 3), so the answer is unique.

word_puzzle.title: False Friends
word_puzzle.body:
Sort these 16 words into four groups of four:

DELTA  ·  MARS  ·  QANTAS  ·  OMEGA
TWIX  ·  MERCURY  ·  LUFTHANSA  ·  FLAKE
SIGMA  ·  VENUS  ·  EMIRATES  ·  BOUNTY
KAPPA  ·  SATURN  ·  RYANAIR  ·  AERO
word_puzzle.approach: Sort the 16 words into four groups of four. Two words look like they belong in a group they don't — spot the decoys.
word_puzzle.answer:
Chocolate bars: BOUNTY, TWIX, FLAKE, AERO
Planets: MERCURY, VENUS, SATURN, MARS
Greek letters: DELTA, SIGMA, OMEGA, KAPPA
Airlines: EMIRATES, QANTAS, RYANAIR, LUFTHANSA

The decoys: MARS is a famous chocolate bar but here it is a planet; DELTA is a major airline but here it is a Greek letter.
